projects.projectName: Vivli Inc - AI Form Check Validation & Agentic Chat Automation

details: Client aligns as Vivli / Vivli Inc.
Historical intelligence refers to the same project family and execution window.
Lifecycle context aligns with Build & Test to PAT transition.
Minor naming variance exists between project labels, but scope, timeline, client, and risk themes are materially consistent.

items.field: Formal PAT acceptance criteria / success thresholds

predictedRisks.riskTitle: PAT and Go-Live Delay from Unresolved Client Dependencies on the Critical Path
predictedRisks.riskDescription: Unresolved client-owned decisions and environment/process dependencies may delay Sprint 5 completion, reduce PAT readiness, and push regression or go-live dates further out.
predictedRisks.rootCause: High-severity client dependencies remain unresolved late in the lifecycle, including chat-based escalation requirements, Azure monitoring/escalation process, dedicated automation testing environment, and Guru Card fit assessment.
triggerConditions: Sprint 5 starts with unresolved client decisions
Automation testing environment remains unavailable or delayed
Azure monitoring/escalation process is not confirmed before PAT
Chat escalation requirements remain unclear during final integration
Guru Card fit assessment remains pending near integrated demo or PAT

potentialImpact.schedule: PAT start or completion may slip, compressing regression and delaying deployment beyond the currently planned October timeline.
potentialImpact.cost: Extended delivery effort may increase unplanned staffing and governance costs.
potentialImpact.quality: Incomplete dependency closure can force partial testing or late fixes under compressed timelines.
potentialImpact.customer: Stakeholder confidence may reduce if the integrated workflow is not demo-ready or PAT-ready on time.
potentialImpact.operations: Production readiness and support preparation may be delayed.

supportingPatterns: Client dependency bottleneck recurs across delivery stages
Customer feedback and client environment dependency delayed prior validation windows
Early dependency-related slippage compounded later-stage schedule compression

mitigationPlan: Escalate all four high-severity client dependencies through weekly governance with dated owners and closure deadlines.
Convert open client decisions into a formal dependency burn-down with daily tracking until Sprint 5 stabilization.
Sequence Sprint 5 work so blocked items are isolated and non-blocked validation proceeds immediately.
Prepare fallback test and demo scenarios where full dependency resolution is not required for all paths.
recommendations: Trigger executive escalation if any critical dependency remains open at Sprint 5 start.
Publish a dependency-to-milestone traceability view linking each open item to Demo, PAT, Regression, and Go-Live impact.
Require explicit client sign-off dates for chat escalation, monitoring process, and environment readiness.
predictedRisks.reasoning: The project has high schedule pressure, declining momentum, unresolved high-severity client dependencies, and no buffer across PAT and regression. Historical evidence shows the same client feedback and environment dependency themes repeatedly disrupted validation timelines.

projectIndicators: WSR-006: four high-severity dependencies still In Progress
WSR-003: Sprint 5 is yet to start and under review
5 contract weeks remaining versus 11 weeks of scheduled work
historicalReferences: Historical R02: delayed customer feedback impacting sprint validation
Historical R03: environment dependency caused sprint slip

predictedRisks.riskTitle: Extended PAT Cycle Due to UI/UX Defects and Ongoing Feedback-Rework Loop
predictedRisks.riskDescription: The project may enter a prolonged PAT cycle if accumulated UI/usability defects and enhancement-type feedback continue to surface during final validation, causing repeated fix-and-retest iterations.
predictedRisks.rootCause: A meaningful share of current defects are UI-related, some issues are still being classified as enhancements, Sprint 3 PAT review is still in progress, and Sprint 5 is reserved largely for bug fixes and feedback resolution.
triggerConditions: High-priority UI/usability issues remain open entering PAT
PAT identifies defects in integrated workflows or in-flight functionality
Enhancement requests are raised as acceptance blockers
Sprint 3/Sprint 4 review observations carry forward into formal PAT

potentialImpact.schedule: PAT duration may extend or generate rework that compresses or delays regression and go-live.
potentialImpact.cost: Additional QA, development, and business review effort may be required.
potentialImpact.quality: Compressed regression after prolonged PAT can increase defect leakage risk.
potentialImpact.customer: User confidence and acceptance may be weakened if core workflows appear unstable or hard to use.
potentialImpact.operations: Support burden may rise during deployment and hypercare due to unresolved usability issues.

supportingPatterns: Continuous feedback loops improve alignment but can create hidden schedule drag
Delayed customer validation historically affected subsequent implementation
Early slippage and rework patterns now appear as late-stage validation compression

mitigationPlan: Define and approve a PAT defect triage model separating critical defects, acceptable minor defects, and post-go-live enhancements.
Prioritize closure of UI/usability defects affecting primary researcher/member journeys before formal PAT start.
Run a pre-PAT integrated workflow rehearsal using business scenarios to flush defects early.
Freeze non-essential enhancements and limit PAT scope to agreed acceptance-critical capabilities.
recommendations: Create a business-approved severity rubric for PAT findings.
Use daily defect aging and retest dashboards during PAT.
Ensure front-end automation focus covers the highest-volume rule and usability paths first.
predictedRisks.reasoning: Project evidence shows UI-related bugs form a good percentage of the backlog, PAT feedback is already active, and Sprint 5 is focused on bug fixes. Historical intelligence confirms that delayed client validation and feedback dependence recur in this project context.
monitoringIndicators: Defect aging and retest pass rate
Volume of enhancement requests raised during validation
Sprint 3 and Sprint 4 PAT closure status

projectIndicators: WSR-008: UI-related bugs represent a good percent of defects
WSR-009: 21 items in Dev Validation and 7 Ready for test
WSR-010: Sprint 3 PAT Early Access Review still in progress
WSR-004: Sprint 5 includes bug fixes and enhancement feedback
historicalReferences: Historical R02: customer feedback delay impacted validation and implementation
Historical lessons: continuous feedback loops can prolong acceptance without fixed scope boundaries

predictedRisks.riskTitle: Regression and Deployment Slippage from Zero-Buffer Critical Path
predictedRisks.riskDescription: Any material defect discovery or rework during PAT may immediately compress the fixed regression window and delay deployment because the current critical path has little to no schedule buffer.
predictedRisks.rootCause: The remaining plan contains tightly sequenced milestones—Sprint 5, PAT, code freeze, regression, deployment, and hypercare—with no meaningful slack, while schedule health is already under review and work completion trails elapsed time.
triggerConditions: Critical or high defects are found late in PAT
PAT completion slips beyond September 18
Regression entry is delayed by unresolved acceptance issues
Integrated workflow defects require code changes after planned code freeze

potentialImpact.schedule: Regression may be shortened or deployment delayed beyond October 16.
potentialImpact.cost: Recovery actions may require overtime, extended team allocation, or parallel support effort.
potentialImpact.quality: Shortened regression can reduce test coverage and increase release risk.
potentialImpact.customer: Go-live commitments may become unstable or require expectation resets.
potentialImpact.operations: Operational readiness, training, and hypercare planning may be disrupted.

supportingPatterns: Validation effort expands beyond original baseline
Early sprint slippage compounds into late-stage compression
Schedule adaptation occurred previously without eliminating structural causes

mitigationPlan: Define non-negotiable PAT exit criteria and a contingency plan for partial defect carry-forward with business approval.
Start regression preparation assets and scenario packs before PAT completes.
Reserve contingency capacity for defect turnaround during PAT-to-regression transition.
Re-baseline milestone dependencies weekly based on actual defect trends.
recommendations: Introduce a formal decision gate at PAT midpoint to assess go-live feasibility.
Protect regression scope around business-critical workflows and security/access paths.
Publish schedule sensitivity analysis showing the effect of 3-day, 5-day, and 10-day PAT slippages.
predictedRisks.reasoning: The project has 11 weeks of remaining work against 5 weeks of contract time, explicit extension pressure, and fixed PAT/regression windows. Historical intelligence shows downstream validation effort was underestimated and later expanded outside the original baseline.

projectIndicators: WSR-005: fixed PAT, Regression, Deployment timeline
Delivery feasibility marks PAT, Regression, and Go-Live as AT RISK
Work completed approximately 60-65% while 68.75% of time has elapsed
historicalReferences: Historical R01: regression testing and extended PAT added after initiation and outside SOW
Enterprise pattern: validation expansion drives contractual and schedule drift

predictedRisks.riskTitle: Late-Stage Technical Change Causes Functional Regression or Security Readiness Delay
predictedRisks.riskDescription: Late implementation of GPT-5 Mini migration, MSAL/RBAC, and related DevOps/IaC sign-off activities in Sprint 5 may introduce defects, revalidation effort, or readiness delays close to PAT and release.
predictedRisks.rootCause: Multiple technically significant changes are scheduled in the final build sprint rather than earlier stabilization windows, increasing the probability of regression, integration instability, or incomplete validation.
triggerConditions: GPT-5 Mini migration changes response behavior or validation accuracy
MSAL/RBAC implementation affects admin or user access flows
DevOps IaC sign-off identifies infrastructure or configuration gaps
Integration of chat escalation workflow creates unexpected failures

potentialImpact.schedule: Additional fix cycles may delay PAT entry or prolong regression.
potentialImpact.cost: Specialist engineering and validation effort may increase late in delivery.
potentialImpact.quality: Functional regression, access-control defects, or model-behavior variance may reduce release confidence.
potentialImpact.customer: User acceptance may be affected if role access or AI behavior changes unexpectedly.
potentialImpact.operations: Production support and security readiness may be weakened if release controls are incomplete.

supportingPatterns: Progressive scope clarification continues late into execution
Additional technical requirements emerged beyond original baseline
Underestimated downstream effort has repeatedly increased volatility

mitigationPlan: Separate Sprint 5 technical changes into must-have versus deferrable items before PAT commitment.
Execute targeted regression packs for AI behavior, authorization, and integrated workflow paths immediately after each technical change.
Require explicit security/access acceptance for RBAC flows before PAT start.
Baseline pre- and post-migration functional metrics for GPT-5 Mini behavior.
recommendations: Defer non-essential model or platform changes if they are not release-critical.
Create rollback and feature-toggle strategies for migration and access-control changes.
Ensure DevOps, QA, and business leads sign off a late-change risk review before code freeze.
predictedRisks.reasoning: Sprint 5 includes multiple complex technical changes—GPT migration, MSAL/RBAC, escalation workflow integration, and IaC sign-off—at a point where the project is already under schedule pressure. This combination creates concentrated late-stage delivery risk.

projectIndicators: WSR-004: Sprint 5 includes MSAL/RBAC, GPT-5 Mini migration, DevOps IaC sign-off
Current drift analysis highlights added security and technology requirements late in execution
Remaining work complexity assessed as HIGH
historicalReferences: Historical R03: broader scope and dependencies caused slip
Historical lessons: late-stage technology and security additions increase volatility

predictedRisks.riskTitle: Contractual and Resource Ambiguity Disrupts Post-September Delivery Continuity
predictedRisks.riskDescription: Because critical delivery phases extend beyond the original contract end date without documented formal amendment, the project may face delayed decisions, funding ambiguity, or resource continuity issues during PAT, regression, deployment, or hypercare.
predictedRisks.rootCause: The operating timeline now runs approximately 7 weeks beyond the contract baseline, but no formal extension, revised budget, or confirmed resource commitment is documented.
triggerConditions: No contract amendment is executed before September 11, 2026
Budget approval for extended effort remains unclear
Key team members are not committed through October 30, 2026
Client approval of the extended timeline remains informal

potentialImpact.schedule: Decision delays or resourcing gaps may affect regression, deployment, or hypercare continuity.
potentialImpact.cost: Unfunded effort or disputed charges may emerge.
potentialImpact.quality: Resource turnover or reduced continuity can lower defect resolution efficiency.
potentialImpact.customer: Trust may erode if timeline and commercial expectations are misaligned.
potentialImpact.operations: Hypercare readiness and transition to steady-state support may be weakened.

supportingPatterns: Validation effort expanded outside original baseline
Operational extension occurred without governance closure
Administrative mitigation did not resolve structural exposure

mitigationPlan: Execute a formal contract amendment covering timeline, scope treatment, budget, and acceptance implications.
Confirm named resource commitments through the revised end date.
Align milestone/payment treatment with the revised delivery plan.
Document client approval of the revised plan and go-live governance gates.
recommendations: Escalate this item to PMR/Steering immediately rather than treating it as an operational note.
Add a commercial-readiness checkpoint before PAT exit.
Document clear ownership for budget, contract, and resource continuity decisions.
predictedRisks.reasoning: The extension is already evidenced in the live plan, but not formally documented. Historical intelligence shows this exact risk pattern recurred and was never fully resolved through governance controls.

projectIndicators: Extension impact identifies high contractual impact and unclear budget/resource commitment
historicalReferences: Historical R01: regression/PAT additions outside original SOW caused contractual ambiguity and unplanned effort
Historical assessment: mitigation incomplete and governance closure ineffective
